source_exclusion_rationale: The package.json files list publishes build and src while explicitly excluding src/__tests__. This benchmark uses exactly the implementation-source part of that published package. No production file is excluded. Tests remain source-review references and their complete excluded inventory is retained.
freeze_status: source-author complete; independent source review and committed selection/configuration freeze required before retrieval, indexing or inference
split_policy: All 14 queries are fresh repository holdout data for this project. Neither labels nor TanStack Query retrieval outcomes may choose ranking, selection rules, budgets, prompts or thresholds. Freeze labels, independently reviewed source, implementation and configuration before evaluation. Model pretraining may include TanStack Query; this is not model-pretraining isolation.
target_groups_semantics: OR within each evidence group, AND across every group. Every OR alternative names an actual extracted ancestor or nested implementation containing exactly the same full physical evidence interval and bytes. A result must contain that entire interval, match its qualified symbol and source hash. Group labels never credit a mere symbol hit or an unrelated window of the same long function.

queries.query: Where does a fetch reuse an already running request instead of starting duplicate work, then publish successful data to the observer update path and cache success callbacks?
queries.notes: The early fetch branch continues allowed retries and returns the current retryer promise when it can reuse active work. The later success path awaits the retryer, rejects undefined data, commits data, and invokes cache callbacks. Query.setData (read as linkage context) dispatches success; the dispatch tail calls each observer, whose update hook refreshes its result and timers. Every group is required to connect request reuse, completion, cache callbacks and observer delivery. The label does not claim cancelRefetch always reuses a request: the earlier branch explicitly handles cancellation separately.

queries.query: When the last observer leaves, where does reading the query signal determine whether to cancel the running transport or only stop retries, and how does cancellation restore state and abort the controller?
queries.notes: Removing the final observer distinguishes an actually consumed AbortSignal from unused transport cancellation. The signal getter records consumption; retryer.cancel rejects with CancelledError and invokes onCancel; that callback restores the saved state with idle fetch status when revert is requested, then aborts. Both sides of the callback boundary and both signal paths are required. This is a query lifecycle label, not a claim that every transport honors AbortSignal.

packages/query-core/src/__tests__/query.test.tsx::should continue if cancellation is not supported and signal is not consumed

queries.query: Where are mutations sharing a scope prevented from executing in parallel, and how is another paused mutation in that scope continued when the current one finishes, including failure?
queries.notes: Mutation.execute gives the retryer a canRun callback into the cache. The cache allows only the first pending member of a named scope (or any unscoped mutation). execute finally invokes runNext regardless of its success/error branch; the cache finds a different paused member of that scope and calls continue. Mutation.continue and retryer.pause/continue were read as linkage context. No ordering among different scopes is asserted.

queries.query: Where does invalidating cached queries mark their state stale, optionally skip refetching entirely, and otherwise refetch matching queries while excluding disabled or static ones?
queries.notes: The client first invalidates every matched query, has the explicit none escape hatch, and derives the refetch type. Query.invalidate dispatches only when not already invalidated. The refetch path applies disabled/static filters before fetch, defaults cancelRefetch, handles throwOnError, and does not wait for paused fetches. Query.#dispatch invalidation, Query.isDisabled and Query.isStatic were read as linkage context. This label concerns the client orchestration and actual query state transition rather than defining all matching-filter semantics.

packages/query-core/src/__tests__/query.test.tsx::should not change state on invalidate() if already invalidated

queries.query: Where are forward and backward page fetches added together with their page parameters, and where does a page limit drop entries from the opposite end in each direction?
queries.notes: The direction branch chooses the previous/next parameter and passes its backward flag into fetchPage. After the query resolves, fetchPage chooses the append or prepend helper and applies it equally to pages and pageParams with maxPages. The two utility implementations slice opposing ends of the new arrays when over the maximum. The next/previous parameter resolver implementations were read as linkage context; no behavior of an application-supplied parameter callback is assumed.

queries.query: With optimistic results and rendering-time prefetching enabled, where is the predicted pending or fetching result constructed, and how does its exposed promise later settle and remove its pending resolvers?
queries.notes: createResult conditionally overlays fetchState before the actual fetch and fetchState derives pending/fetching versus paused state. The experimental prefetch-in-render block finalizes or recreates the result thenable from data/error. pendingThenable.finalize and its resolve/reject methods update status/value/reason and delete both pending callbacks. The remainder of the createResult switch was read: pending same-query promises are finalized, fulfilled/rejected promises are recreated on incompatible next results. This is conditional behavior under both named options, not a promise-settlement guarantee for every observer configuration.

queries.query: Where does hydration attach a dehydrated pending promise with data deserialization, and where is that supplied promise reused for the first execution instead of calling the query function again?
queries.notes: The hydration branch checks existing pending/fetching state and dehydration time before passing Promise.resolve(promise).then(deserializeData) as initialPromise to query.fetch. fetch forwards it to the retryer. The retry loop uses that initialPromise only at failureCount zero and otherwise calls config.fn. The full hydration implementation was read to establish the skip conditions and data timestamps. This does not claim that retry attempts can never run the query function or that an older dehydrated promise replaces newer cached data.

queries.query: Where is an observer selector result reused when both its input and selector are unchanged, and where are equal nested arrays or objects reused when a newly selected result needs structural sharing?
queries.notes: The observer compares the data reference and selector function, reuses its memoized selection, or calls select and replaceData. replaceData honors a supplied sharing function, otherwise uses replaceEqualDeep unless sharing is disabled. The recursive routine preserves equal children and returns the entire previous value only when sizes and equal-child counts agree. It is structural sharing for plain arrays/objects and does not promise value equality semantics for every JavaScript object.

queries.query: Where are plain-object keys sorted recursively while serializing a query key so that different property insertion orders produce the same cache hash?
queries.notes: hashKey uses a JSON replacer that sorts the keys of each plain object; nested objects pass through the same replacer. Array order is preserved. The label does not claim a collision-free hash or serialization of arbitrary cyclic values.

queries.query: Where does partial query-key matching recursively require every key of the requested subset to match the corresponding value in a larger key?
queries.notes: The matcher accepts direct equality, rejects differing types, and recursively checks Object.keys(b) against a when both are non-null objects. This is directional subset matching, not symmetric deep equality.

queries.query: Where does nested notification batching decrement its transaction count even if a callback throws, and flush queued notifications only after the outermost batch exits?
queries.notes: The batch method increments transactions, invokes its callback in try/finally, decrements in finally, and flushes only when the count reaches zero. schedule and flush were read as linkage context. This control asks for transaction exit behavior, not the scheduler implementation.

queries.notes: updateGcTime takes Math.max of the previous duration and the newly supplied duration or environment-specific default. This does not require the separate timeout provider or actual removal implementation.

queries.query: Where does this query-core package persist its cache to disk by writing a temporary file and atomically replacing the old cache file?
queries.notes: No filesystem cache writer, temporary-file lifecycle, rename/replace operation or filesystem import is implemented in the pinned core source. The persister option delegates to caller-supplied functions and does not implement disk persistence. Optional persister packages elsewhere in the upstream monorepo are outside this explicitly scoped package.

queries.query: Where does this query-core package broadcast cache updates between browser tabs over BroadcastChannel and apply updates received from other tabs?
queries.notes: The included package has local cache listeners, online/focus browser event managers and notification scheduling, but no BroadcastChannel or cross-tab send/receive transport. A separate broadcast client package exists elsewhere upstream and is outside this package scope; this absence is not a claim about the entire monorepo.
